description:
Redwood Inference is expanding enterprise-ready security controls across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This project standardizes the audit log event schema across the product surface area and drives instrumentation to reach 100% coverage for “sensitive actions” (actions that materially impact customer data access, security posture, billing, or availability).

Goals:
- Define and publish a canonical, versioned audit event schema (naming, required fields, actor/target modeling, request correlation, error semantics).
- Build/extend shared libraries for emitting and validating events across services (API gateway, console backend, RBAC/auth, deployment controllers, private installer).
- Create a single inventory of sensitive actions and map each to one or more audit events; enforce coverage via CI checks and dashboards.
- Ensure audit logs are reliable (delivery lag SLO, retry semantics), queryable, and exportable (S3/SIEM/webhook) with clear retention/redaction guidance.

Scope:
- In-scope sensitive actions include: auth/RBAC changes, API key creation/rotation/revocation, user/admin management, org/workspace settings, model deployment/rollout actions, routing policy changes, dedicated capacity scaling and quota changes, private deployment install/upgrade/rollback, data retention changes, and audit log configuration changes.
- Out of scope initially: non-sensitive observability events, full historical backfill for all legacy logs (limited migration/backfill only where required for customer contract), and customer-specific custom event formats.

Stakeholders and roles:
- Product owner: Naomi Feldman (Director of Product, Security & Compliance).
- Security engineering owner: Marcus Lin (Director, Security Engineering) with oversight from Dr. Aisha Rahman (CISO).
- GRC/compliance alignment: Olga Petrov (GRC Director) to map schema/coverage to SOC 2/ISO evidence expectations.
- Engineering execution: Platform/Telemetry (e.g., Nadia Rahman), SRE (Rafael Mendes, Miles Thornton), Private Deployments, Console/Tooling, and Runtime teams.

Phases and timeline (typical 2-quarter execution):
1) Discovery + inventory (2–3 weeks): enumerate sensitive actions, audit existing logging, define acceptance criteria.
2) Schema v1 + libraries (3–5 weeks): publish schema, implement validators, add developer guidance.
3) Instrumentation + migration (6–10 weeks): service-by-service coverage work, legacy event normalization, add automated tests.
4) Reliability + reporting (3–6 weeks): delivery lag SLO, dashboards, coverage reports, exporter hardening.
5) Beta + launch (3–6 weeks): select enterprise customers, security review collateral, runbook/training, GA rollout.

Key deliverables:
- Confluence standards/specs, PRD, runbooks, and compliance control mapping.
- Linear plan (initiative + workstream tickets), GitHub PRs implementing schema/coverage, and Slack decision threads.
- Support artifacts (Jira tickets) and customer-facing readiness (Fireflies/Gmail/HubSpot artifacts referencing audit log requirements).

files.description: Program overview: goals, definition of “sensitive action,” in-scope systems, owners, and rollout phases; links to schema, inventory, and coverage dashboards.
Canonical audit event schema v1: required fields (event_name, actor, target, org, request_id, ip/user_agent, outcome), versioning strategy, examples, and backward-compat rules.
Master inventory of sensitive actions across API/Console/Dedicated/Private with a mapping table to expected audit events; includes owners and coverage status.
Coverage policy: what “100% coverage” means, CI gates (schema validation + action inventory checks), exceptions process, and required test cases.
Threat model for audit logging: tampering, bypass, spoofing, PII leakage; controls like append-only storage, signing, least-privilege access, and redaction.
Migration plan from legacy/partial audit events to schema v1: rename map, deprecation windows, dual-write strategy, and customer communication notes.
SOC 2/ISO evidence mapping: which schema fields and coverage reports satisfy control requirements; evidence collection procedure and auditor-friendly exports.
Engineering standard for audit log telemetry: correlation IDs, retry semantics, metric names, delivery lag SLO, and required dashboards/alerts.
Naming conventions for audit events (verbs, resources, namespace rules), reserved fields, and examples to prevent inconsistent event taxonomies.
System doc for the audit log pipeline (ingest → validate → store → export): components, dependencies, scaling, and failure modes.
Runbook for audit log delivery lag/errors: dashboards, common causes (queue backlog, exporter failures), mitigation steps, and escalation paths.
Policy defining who can access raw audit logs internally, approval workflow for restricted access, and logging/monitoring of internal audit log queries.
PRD: customer requirements (SIEM export, retention, filtering), success metrics, beta plan, and GA acceptance criteria for audit logs.
Sales/security enablement FAQ: what’s logged, schema stability/versioning, retention/export options, and common enterprise questionnaire answers.
Initiative setup: “Audit log schema standardization + coverage” — milestones, release plan, beta criteria, and cross-team commitments.
Beta program ticket: identify 3–5 enterprise design partners, define feedback rubric (schema usability, completeness, export performance), and success gates.
Packaging decision ticket: audit log export options (S3/webhook/Splunk), retention tiers, and any compliance add-on implications.
Design task: Console “Audit Logs” page UX (filters, export, field display), empty states, and admin-only access handling.
Define schema v1 + examples: event envelope, actor/target model, error/outcome semantics; includes review checklist from Security + Telemetry.
Implement shared audit logging library + schema validator used by services; add lint rule to block unregistered event names.
Instrumentation: API key create/rotate/revoke events across hosted API and console; ensure request_id + actor propagation.
Instrumentation: RBAC policy bundle updates (role create/update/delete, permission changes), including “who changed what” diffs.
Instrumentation: model deployment and rollout actions (canary start/stop, pin/unpin versions, fallback policy changes).
Instrumentation: Dedicated capacity scaling and quota/admin changes; include before/after values and source of change (auto/manual).
Instrumentation: Private deployment installer/upgrade/rollback events, including package version, operator identity, and cluster id.
Exporter hardening: audit-log-exporter reliability (retries, backpressure), delivery metrics, and configurable sink destinations.
Observability work: add delivery lag SLO, dashboards, and paging policy; define what constitutes “drop” vs “delay.”
Legacy migration: dual-write old/new event names, then cutover; add deprecation warnings and customer-facing change notes.
Coverage scanner: automated report comparing sensitive action inventory vs emitted/validated events; outputs coverage % by subsystem.
Integration tests: end-to-end tests that perform sensitive actions and assert audit events exist with required fields.
Console backend: Audit Logs API (filtering, pagination, RBAC enforcement); includes performance considerations and rate limiting.
Hotfix/bug: missing audit events for API token rotation in one code path; triggered by support escalation and linked incident notes.
PR: Add audit event schema v1 definitions (JSONSchema) and shared helper types; includes initial validator and unit tests.
PR: Introduce audit-event registry + build-time check to prevent unregistered event names; updates developer docs in-repo.
PR: Emit audit events for API key create/revoke/rotate; propagates actor identity and request_id through gateway to services.
PR: Add RBAC change auditing (role/permission updates) and include diff payload; includes redaction of sensitive fields.
PR: Model rollout actions now emit audit logs (canary toggles, pin/unpin); includes backwards-compat mapping to legacy events.
PR: Add audit log delivery metrics (enqueue, persisted, exported) and a delivery-lag histogram; wires to observability pipeline.
PR: Add audit log integration test harness that performs sensitive actions in staging and asserts event presence/fields.
PR: Dual-write legacy and schema-v1 event names for selected actions; adds config flag to cut over per environment.
PR: Console backend Audit Logs API endpoints (list/filter/export token issuance); enforces admin RBAC and rate limits.
PR: Dedicated scaling actions now generate audit events; includes before/after desired capacity and initiator (auto/manual).
PR: Add audit log coverage scanner job and CI gate for new sensitive actions; posts coverage summary in build output.
PR: Exporter retry/backoff and dead-letter queue support; adds per-sink delivery metrics and structured error reporting.
PR: Add Grafana dashboards + alerts for audit log delivery lag and drop rate; includes suggested paging thresholds.
PR: Add explicit permissions for Audit Logs API and export actions; updates default roles and migration notes.
PR: Emit audit events for private install/upgrade/rollback operations; includes operator identity and cluster metadata.
PR: Hotfix for missing audit event on one API token rotation code path; adds regression test and incident reference.
PR: Add redaction rules for audit payloads (no secrets/tokens); includes tests ensuring sensitive keys are scrubbed.
Thread coordinating schema v1 requirements: required fields, actor model, and what qualifies as a sensitive action; includes review comments from Security Eng and Product.
Thread debating event naming conventions and namespace boundaries (api.*, console.*, rbac.*); ends with a lightweight decision and follow-ups.
Thread on implementation details: where schema validation happens (service vs pipeline), performance overhead concerns, and sampling (rejected for audit logs).
Thread defining delivery lag SLO and alert thresholds; includes links to a draft dashboard and runbook steps.
Thread: how to audit model rollout actions initiated by runtime controllers vs console; clarifies actor attribution and service identity.
Thread triaging a customer report that audit logs missed API key rotation events; links Jira SUP ticket and the eventual hotfix PR.
Incident-related thread: audit-log exporter backlog causing delayed delivery; includes mitigation (scale consumers) and follow-up tasks.
Thread reviewing payload redaction rules and internal access policy; includes questions about IP/user-agent retention and privacy constraints.
Thread aligning PM/Eng on beta scope, which events must be ready for enterprise security review, and communication plan.
Customer ticket: enterprise prospect requests confirmation of audit log coverage for API key rotation and RBAC changes; includes questionnaires and follow-up links.
Customer ticket: audit logs missing some admin actions in Dedicated (capacity scaling); investigation notes and link to instrumentation PR.
Customer ticket: SIEM export intermittently failing (S3 sink); includes logs, exporter retry discussion, and resolution via exporter PR.
Internal support ticket: request for restricted access to raw audit logs for incident investigation; documents approval and access grant per policy.
Working spreadsheet (table-style): sensitive actions list, expected event names, owning service/team, current coverage status, and notes on gaps.
Draft review doc: open questions, contentious fields (targets, IP), and proposed compromises before Confluence publication.
Tracker for beta design partners: who requested which events/exports, status, dates of enablement, and feedback snippets.
SRE working sheet: delivery lag baseline, proposed SLO, alert thresholds, and expected load; includes links to dashboards.
Security review call transcript with an enterprise prospect focused on audit log completeness, schema stability, export formats, and retention controls.
Technical deep dive transcript: customer SIEM integration expectations (Splunk/S3/webhook), performance requirements, and failure handling.
Internal kickoff transcript: roles, timeline, and agreement on ‘inventory first’ approach; includes action items for schema and instrumentation workstreams.
Email thread: coordinating audit log beta with Sales/SE—customer asks, timeline expectations, and links to PRD/FAQ drafts (internal participants limited to allowed mailboxes).
Email thread: executive-level escalation on audit log contract language and evidence expectations; loops in GRC and Security Eng for sign-off.
Email thread: customer security questionnaire follow-up focused on audit log coverage guarantees and access controls; includes attachment stubs for FAQ/PRD excerpts.
HubSpot company record: enterprise prospect requiring SOC 2-style audit logs + SIEM export; notes on required events, retention, and blockers.
HubSpot company record: regulated customer evaluating Private deployment; highlights on-prem constraints and audit log requirements tied to admin actions and upgrades.
HubSpot company record: Dedicated customer expansion where audit log export is a procurement prerequisite; includes activity timeline linking calls/emails/support tickets.
